editorial:
Imagine stepping into a world where scary movies are the only thing that matters. You get to hang out with the wild crowd at the Horror-on-Sea festival in Essex, where the vibe is all about loving the strange and the spooky. Alexander Churchyard takes you behind the scenes to show how this event grew over thirteen years. You will meet the organizers and the fans who treat this place like a second home. It feels less like a stiff documentary and more like a home movie made by people who truly love the genre. It is a great look at how a small community can build something huge just by sharing a passion for gore and screams.

What really works here is the energy. The pacing stays quick, and the interviews are honest and funny. You get to see the blood, the guts, and the laughs that happen when horror fans get together. If you are not into indie films, it might feel a bit niche, but for anyone who likes the weird side of cinema, it is a goldmine.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing a huge celebration of the festival's thirteenth anniversary. It ends with a montage of the best moments from the past decade, showing how the event evolved from a small gathering to a major attraction. The final scenes focus on the future, promising that the festival will keep running. It concludes with a heartfelt message about how horror brings people together, leaving you feeling happy and hyped for next year.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror movies and indie film festivals.
